<description>
In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error reply with the id and version of the element before it.

`ExecuteHTTPRPC` uses one request object for the whole batch. `parse()` throws on a non-object before it resets `id` and `m_json_version`. For `[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"getblockcount","id":"X"}, 2]` the reply has two objects with `"id":"X"`, one with a result and one with an error. If the first element is a notification, the error is dropped. I reset both fields at the top of `parse()`, so the error is the one the first element of a batch already gets. The new case in `interface_rpc.py` fails on master and passes with this change.

This is one of several PRs from a large audit of Bitcoin Core that I did with the help of LLM tools. The audit produced its evidence all at once, which is why the PRs arrive together. I understand each change fully and will answer review questions myself.
</description>

<commits>
0811092e11 rpc: reset id and version per batch element

In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error
reply with the id and version of the element before it. A client that
matches replies by id can take that error for the result of the
previous call. If the previous element was a 2.0 notification, the
error is dropped.

I reset both at the start of JSONRPCRequest::parse(). The functional
test covers the two cases.
</commits>

<patch>
diff --git a/src/rpc/request.cpp b/src/rpc/request.cpp
index f348ed983e..6fcf5f01e8 100644
--- a/src/rpc/request.cpp
+++ b/src/rpc/request.cpp
@@ -200,6 +200,11 @@ std::vector<UniValue> JSONRPCProcessBatchReply(const UniValue& in)
 
 void JSONRPCRequest::parse(const UniValue& valRequest)
 {
+    // Start from the defaults, so that an error reply to a request that is
+    // not an object does not carry the id or version of a previous request
+    id = UniValue::VNULL;
+    m_json_version = JSONRPCVersion::V1_LEGACY;
+
     // Parse request
     if (!valRequest.isObject())
         throw JSONRPCError(RPC_INVALID_REQUEST, "Invalid Request object");
diff --git a/test/functional/interface_rpc.py b/test/functional/interface_rpc.py
index d9636c122a..3fa758ecb5 100755
--- a/test/functional/interface_rpc.py
+++ b/test/functional/interface_rpc.py
@@ -176,6 +176,19 @@ class RPCInterfaceTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
             request_fields={"jsonrpc": "2.1"},
             response_fields={"result": None, "error": {"code": RPC_INVALID_REQUEST, "message": "JSON-RPC version not supported"}}))
 
+    def test_batch_invalid_element_reply(self):
+        self.log.info("Testing that an invalid batch element does not reuse the id or version of the previous one...")
+        invalid_element = {"result": None, "error": {"code": RPC_INVALID_REQUEST, "message": "Invalid Request object"}, "id": None}
+
+        response, status = send_json_rpc(self.nodes[0], [{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "getblockcount", "id": "X"}, 2])
+        assert_equal(status, 200)
+        assert_equal(response, [{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "result": 0, "id": "X"}, invalid_element])
+
+        # The error is not mistaken for a reply to the notification before it
+        response, status = send_json_rpc(self.nodes[0], [{"jsonrpc": "2.0", "method": "getblockcount"}, 2])
+        assert_equal(status, 200)
+        assert_equal(response, [invalid_element])
+
     def test_http_status_codes(self):
         self.log.info("Testing HTTP status codes for JSON-RPC 1.1 requests...")
         # OK
@@ -240,6 +253,7 @@ class RPCInterfaceTest(BitcoinTestFramework):
     def run_test(self):
         self.test_getrpcinfo()
         self.test_batch_requests()
+        self.test_batch_invalid_element_reply()
         self.test_http_status_codes()
         self.test_work_queue_exceeded()
 

</patch>
